financier: EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
scope_basis: Loan for a telecom operator's fibre, mobile network and submarine cable capital expenditure.
title: EBRD — Tunisie Telecom (Project Hannibal), 2024
description: EBRD Board report (approved 24 July 2024) for Project Hannibal — "a development-linked loan to the Company in the amount of up to EUR 190 million, in four tranches, including a first committed tranche of EUR 50 million." The EBRD Loan is supported by a first-loss EU EFSD+ Digital Transformation guarantee and complemented by an EUR 11 million EU grant. It finances Tunisie Telecom's capital expenditure — connecting households to fibre, upgrading the fibre backbone, transitioning 3G to 4G and 4G+/5G, and participation in the pan-European MEDUSA submarine cable. Tunisie Telecom is 65% state-owned, 35% owned by Emirates International Telecommunications; the operation is the Bank's first Tunisian public-sector project without a sovereign guarantee.

title: European Union (CEF Digital) — ViaTunisia Bizerte–Marseille submarine cable, 2023
description: "The ViaTunisia project has a total budget of €32 million of which €9.6 million funded under the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) Digital programme." The project deploys "a new, direct submarine route between France and Tunisia" (Marseille–Bizerte, 1,050 km, 20 Tb per fibre pair), running 1 March 2023 – 31 August 2025, "undertaken by Orange Wholesale, as coordinator", following the open-access cable model.

scope_basis: GovTech project digitises delivery of social protection and education services.
title: Digital Transformation for User-Centric Public Services
description: The development objective of the GovTech Digital Transformation for User Centric Public Services Project for Tunisia is to improve equitable access to and the quality and accountability of selected Social Protection and Education services through a GovTech approach. It has three components. a) User-Friendly Institutional and Digital Delivery Solutions aims to simplify and digitize key administrative service delivery processes and introduce user-friendly institutional and digital solutions to improve user access and experience, and to address the digital divide; It has three sub-components. (i) Improving Social Protection Delivery Efficiency, Accountability and User-Friendliness; (ii) Improved Education Delivery Efficiency, Accountability, and User-Friendliness; and (iii) Improving Access and Quality for All : Digitized Access Points promoting digital inclusion; Second component, Public and Private Sector Capabilities for Speedier and Responsive Service Delivery complements first component by strengthening public and private sector capabilities for speedier and more responsive service delivery, with a focus on the two target sectors and four flagship programs; It has three sub-components. (i) Improving User-Oriented Identification and Interoperability; (ii) Improving Service Performance and Citizen Engagement; and (iii) Strengthening Capacity and Change Management; Third Component, Reinforcing Connectivity in Education and Social Protection for more Equitable Access to and Quality of Services seeks to accelerate implementation of the solutions provided under first and second component by stimulating targeted, efficient and private-sector-driven investments to address current inequitable access to and weak quality of indoor and outdoor connectivity at the level of frontline service providers, especially in the lagging areas.
original_amount: USD 100,000,000 (commitment, net of 0 negative type-2 transactions)

title: AFD — Tunisia E-Santé programme loan, 2019
description:
"L'Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) a approuvé, lors d'une séance plénière tenue le jeudi 12 février 2026, le projet de loi portant approbation de l'avenant n°2, signé le 27 décembre 2024, à la convention de prêt conclue le 14 février 2019 entre la République tunisienne et l'Agence française de développement, en vue de contribuer au financement du programme de soutien à la santé électronique «E-Santé»."

"[...] la convention de prêt initiale, portant sur un financement de 27,3 millions d'euros [...]. Concrètement, ce programme repose sur trois axes majeurs, d'abord, la modernisation et la sécurisation des systèmes d'information des établissements de santé, accompagnées de leur déploiement dans 24 hôpitaux universitaires. Ensuite, le soutien au développement et à la mise en œuvre de cinq initiatives régionales de télémédecine [...]. Pour compléter le dispositif, le programme prévoit un renforcement institutionnel dans le domaine de la santé électronique."

"À ce jour, les tirages effectués sur le prêt représentent environ 16%, tandis que le montant restant à mobiliser, objet du présent avenant au titre de la deuxième tranche, est estimé à 23 millions d'euros."

scope_basis: Statistics and open data dissemination are two components; another supports macroeconomic and structural policy design.
title: Tunisia - Supporting the Design & Imlementation of Economic & Social Reforms for Inclusive Growth
description: The present Supporting the Design and Implementation of Economic and Social Reforms for Inclusive Growth is an assistance of the African Development Bank and the OECD to mobilize a grant from the MENA Transition Fund (MENA-TF) in favor of Tunisia. It aims to support the Government of Tunisia (GoT)’s efforts to achieve accelerated and inclusive growth through more efficient planning, design, execution, and monitoring and evaluation capacity of projects and reforms. Notably, the project presents a perfect opportunity to support Tunisia’s efforts to achieve its economic transition and transformation. In particular, the objectives and activities planned under this project makes it a suitable candidate for financing by the MENA Transition Fund given the Fund’s objective of assisting countries in transition to develop inclusive growth and foster home-grown reforms. It will be executed over a period of 36 months, and will comprise four components: (1) Support to the design and implementation of macro-economic and structural policies; (2) Support to inclusive regional development through improved regional statistics and M&E capacity; (3) Support Tunisia’s open data agenda through a new statistical dissemination infrastructure; and (4) Project management and audit. The objective of this project is to support more effective implementation of the GoT’s 5-year plan 2016-2020 and structural reforms by strengthening its capacity in statistics, monitoring and evaluation. Notably, the project presents a perfect opportunity to support Tunisia’s efforts to achieve its economic transition and transformation. In particular, the objectives and activities planned under this project makes it a suitable candidate for financing by the MENA Transition Fund given the Fund’s objective of assisting countries in transition to develop inclusive growth and foster home-grown reforms. The main beneficiary of the project is the Government of Tunisia.
